extracted.intended_audience: members of the London Mathematical Society; academic mathematicians (researchers, postgraduate students) and those applying for society-funded events, jobs, fellowships, and grants
extracted.subtask_description: A society newsletter listing meetings, conferences, workshops, jobs, fellowships, prize citations, funding initiatives, and procedural rules (tickets, registration, deadlines) relevant to the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lee Kuan Yew Postdoctoral Fellowship — eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited from young and outstanding academics for the Lee Kuan Yew Postdoctoral Fellowship. Candidates should be PhD holders who have obtained their PhD degrees in the last few years. They should hold good academic credentials and have published in international refereed journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship tenable up to 3 years initially (possible 2-year extension). Held concurrently with appointment as research staff working in listed research areas (Applied Mathematics, Applied Probability, Optimization, Financial Mathematics). Tax-free stipend US$1,500/month in addition to gross annual salary ranges given; other employment benefits listed. Applicants should send detailed CV, list of publications (including fax/email) and names/addresses of three referees to the Director, Personnel Department. Closing date: 30 September 1998. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Research Associate/Senior Research Associate — selection criteria (University of Sydney)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference will be given to applicants with expertise in listed areas (Lie and algebraic groups; geometry and topology of manifolds; group representations on cohomology spaces, Schubert varieties; reflection groups, Hecke algebras; quantum groups; discriminant algebras). Applicants should have, or expect to receive shortly, a PhD or equivalent qualification, and should have a strong record of publication of original research in the above areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary scales given and length of appointment stated (initial 12 months with possibility of extension). Applicants must address the selection criteria and submit Reference No, curriculum vitae and names/contacts of two confidential referees to the Personnel Officer. The advertisement notes equal employment opportunity policies and that the University may not proceed with any appointment for financial or other reasons. Closing date provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (JEMS) — publication standards
rubrics_metrics.description: JEMS will publish research articles in all active areas of pure and applied mathematics; these will be selected by a distinguished international board of editors and associate editors for their outstanding quality and interest, according to the highest international standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally substantial survey papers on topics of exceptional impact will also be published. Preferred language of publication is English. Electronic submission is encouraged for speedier handling. JEMS will be available online as well as in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: LMS De Morgan Medal — award rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The De Morgan Medal is awarded for many major contributions across an area (example citation: contributions to theory of numbers and modular forms, broad range of central problems, scholarship and mathematical taste).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award recognizes deep, influential work (examples given: estimates for gaps between primes, distribution of zeros of Poincaré series, cusp forms, Rankin–Selberg method). The citation emphasizes both breadth and seminal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Berwick Prize — awarding basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded on the basis of a representative work (example: a survey article 'Spectral Theory of Higher Order Elliptic Operators') and as recognition of substantial contributions to a field (operator theory, heat semigroups, higher-order operators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize cites clarity of exposition, novelty and imagination in mathematics, and contributions that influence both basic mathematics and applications (e.g., to physics and probability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior Whitehead Prize — awarding rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for notable early-career contributions in specified areas (examples: mathematical theory of superconductivity; high-precision asymptotics; hyperbolic geometry — descriptions of distinctive achievements are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria illustrated include originality, development of new methodologies, resolution of outstanding problems, cross-disciplinary impact and use of sophisticated tools. Prize citations emphasize both technical depth and influence on subsequent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathFit initiative — funding priorities and application modes
rubrics_metrics.description: MathFit supports high-quality interdisciplinary research applying novel mathematical techniques to problems in computer science through responsive mode grants, visiting fellowships and summer schools/workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsive mode grants and visiting fellowships are supported by EPSRC and should be submitted through usual EPSRC channels (no closing dates). Visiting fellowships to support transfer of personnel between complementary departments in different UK universities are particularly welcomed. MathFit summer schools and workshops are supported by LMS and EPSRC with flexible format; deadlines for events (e.g., applications for 1999 events by 9 October 1998) are published. Contact details and web pages with full priorities and how-to-apply information are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMR Summer Schools — participant eligibility and support focus
rubrics_metrics.description: TMR-supported Summer Schools aim to provide training for young researchers (i.e., aged under 35) interested in new trends in representation theory and related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants from EU and associated countries are especially invited. The programme encourages researchers from less-favoured regions and women. Applicants can apply for full support (travel and local expenses). Each School has two parts: a 'Compact Seminar' where young participants take an active role, followed by a 'Workshop' with lectures by leading experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference presentation format and scheduling — 'On the Growth and Form' meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily programme consists of plenary talks, workshop sessions, poster presentations and discussion sessions. Invited talks will be 45 minutes with an additional 15 minutes allocated for questions/discussion. There will be three plenary talks of one hour duration during each morning session. Poster sessions follow lunch and the final plenary is followed by a discussion session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant encouragement for graduate students and young post-doctoral researchers to attend. Registration by e-mail or conference web-site preferred; poster/workshop format open to all participants. Practical details (coffee/lunch/tea times, display of specimens) are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: De Morgan House opening — ticket application and allocation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must apply for tickets for the Opening (Friday) and the Buffet Lunch (Saturday) by e-mail or returning a form to arrive by a specified date (Thursday 8 October).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of space pressure a ballot may be held. If a ballot is necessary, preference for Buffet Lunch tickets will be given to those who are not allocated Opening tickets. Maximum two tickets per applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research students to attend meetings — application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited funds are available to help research students attend LMS meetings. Requests for support and enquiries may be addressed to the named contact (Dr D.J.H. Garling) at De Morgan House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact by e-mail or postal address given; implication that support is discretionary and limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional Courses (ISC) — organizational consultation and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: LMS and EPSRC sponsor Instructional Courses (principal audience: research students). LMS is considering expanding the scheme and seeks membership advice on organization, subject range (including more applied subjects like numerical analysis and computer algebra), scientific planning, geographical distribution and frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members invited to send ideas to the named contact by a specified date (before 30th September 1998). The Durham Symposium Committee with EPSRC representation will manage scientific strategy and will solicit and respond to proposals from the spectrum of pure and applied mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop / conference topical scope — 'Algebraic Geometry and Integrable Systems' (example of topical definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop topics enumerated to define scope: role of Baker functions in completely integrable systems (KdV, KP, sine-Gordon), construction of KdV-type solutions associated with algebraic curves, quantum integrability and non-linear discrete-time integrable equations, role of moduli spaces in supersymmetric gauge or string theories, Seiberg–Witten ansatz connections, and recent work linking form-factors to Baker–Akhiezer functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated overall aim is to consolidate understanding of interactions between algebraic geometry and ideas in integrable systems and mathematical physics; emphasis on algebraic geometric ideas introduced by H.F. Baker and their applications. Organisers and local organisers are named; participant list indicative of target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference / workshop contact and registration requirements (general procedural rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many meetings and workshops (Spitalfields Day, ICMS workshops, Summer Schools, etc.) potential attendees are asked to reserve places or register by contacting the named administrative contact (Tracey Dart, ICMS) or via the conference web-site before a specified deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact telephone, fax and e-mail are provided. For some meetings, registration by e-mail or via web-site is preferred, and deadlines (e.g., before 15 September) are explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic job advertisements — common application materials and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Job ads (postdoctoral, research associate, professorship) require applicants to submit specified materials: curriculum vitae, list of publications, names and contact details of referees, a reference number, and sometimes addressing selection criteria; overseas candidates may send fewer copies as noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be sent to specified university offices or personnel officers by stated closing dates. Some adverts note equal opportunity policies, possible salary scales, length of appointment, and that the institution reserves the right not to proceed with an appointment.
